Did you miss the Mobile gaming news of last month? We got you! Here's the roundup for September 2025.

🗓️ Week 1: September 01 to September 07

The first week of September 2025 delivered a variety of new pre-registrations, global releases, betas, and shutdown news. INFINITY BULLETS, My City, Backyard Football ’99, and Medieval Baghdad launched globally, while Kingdom Rush Battles was confirmed for October.

Pre-registrations opened for BrambleBound, The Ninth Relic, The Kingdom: Medieval Tales, MU: Pocket Knights, Volley Girls, and Girls’ Frontline: Fire Control, alongside Ubisoft’s Might & Magic Fates TCG. Soft launches included Resident Evil Survival Unit, while Ubisoft also rolled out a The Division Resurgence Closed Beta in Romania.

The week also brought major updates like the MLBB M7 World Championship heading to Indonesia, Bandai Namco’s DRAGON BALL Games Battle Hour 2026 announcement, and Nexon addressing the Blue Archive Koyukification hack. On the flip side, shutdowns were confirmed for Ride Kamens and Tarisland.

🗓️ Week 2: September 08 to September 14

The second week of September 2025 had little to share in terms of mobile gaming news. TED Tumblewords, Anchor Panic, and Soccer Manager 2026 went live globally, while Football Manager 26 locked in its November 4 release.

Pre-registration began for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin and Honkai: Nexus Anima, with Com2uS unveiling Star Sailors closed beta and Krafton kicking off Astro Arena alpha testing.

On the soft launch side, Tower Dominion, Golf Star 2, and Police Chief made regional debuts, while Sailing the Winds expanded to iOS. Meanwhile, industry updates included PUBG UNITED 2025 esports unification, Arknights: Endfield early 2026 launch window, and XD Games’ Heartopia announcement for 2026.

🗓️ Week 3: September 15 to September 21

Another decent week, AutoChess Hero, Tom and Jerry Blast, Angry Birds Rush, Shadowborn, and Sunday City entered early access or soft launch, while Elpis: Fallen Star and Katana Dragon confirmed late-September release dates.

UNO Wonder, The Palace on the Hill, Morikomori Life, and Buried Stars also saw mobile debuts. Announcements included DRAGON QUEST Smash/Grow closed beta and a new Hanazono Serena visual novel, while Blue Protocol: Star Resonance locked in October 9 launch.

Pre-registrations also opened for Chess Rumble, Pine Hearts, and Stella Sora, alongside Kakao’s NOVAFRONT soft launch in the Philippines. Apple made headlines with Safari full-screen browser gaming coming in iOS 26.

🗓️ Week 4: September 22 to September 28

The fourth week saw Tower Rush, Motor Speed Traffic 3D, Runes of Legend, and Fire Emblem Shadows launched globally, while Chaos Zero Nightmare and m00m world confirmed October release dates. Pre-registration began for Brave Frontier Versus.

Jurassic War Survival, NOVAFRONT, Inkvasion, and Cross Gate: Adventure got their soft launches. There were some new game announcements: Harukanaru Toki no Naka de winter release, Girls Band Cry: First Riff, and Kadokawa’s Shield Hero game adaptation.

Updates brought ANANTA gameplay reveal, RAVEN2 showcase, Kojima Productions x Niantic collab, Petit Planet from HoYoverse revealed with a closed beta, and Angry Birds’ China comeback. NetEase also confirmed Racing Master’s Latam launch for October 29, while Ninja Arashi 2 expansion paved way for its sequel.

🗓️ Week 5: September 29 to September 30

The short last two days of September brought two major headlines. Electronic Arts confirmed its $55 billion acquisition deal, taking the company private in one of the largest gaming buyouts ever. Meanwhile, HoYoverse filed the “HoYoLand” trademark, sparking speculation on a potential theme park.

If you have until the end and found it useful, feel free to repost this! 

🔗https://t.co/fGeMTqEHIK

data.raw_text:
Long post, patience requested and read through. 

Corruption isn’t an accident in the Philippines. It’s a national inheritance, passed down from one administration to the next. A curse we can’t seem to break. 

The executive branch?
Marcos Sr. family: $5–10B stolen
Estrada: convicted of plunder, later pardoned.
Arroyo: plunder charges on ₱366M PCSO funds, acquitted.

In the Philippines, even plunder comes with a second chance.

The legislature?
The Pork Barrel scam alone bled ₱10B through fake NGOs.
“Budget insertions” & “amendments” is very much alive!

For many lawmakers, Congress isn’t about lawmaking, it’s about looting, it’s business as usual. 

The judiciary?
Ex-CJ Corona hid ₱183M in assets. Ordinary citizens know it: justice here is for sale. Bribes, fixers, and lagay define the courts. I know, I myself am a victim. 

When the last bastion of justice is corrupt, who protects the people?

The World Bank estimates 20% of our annual budget is lost to corruption. That’s hospitals unfunded, flood projects unbuilt, classrooms empty.

Transparency Intl. gave PH 34/100 in its 2024 corruption index, among Asia’s worst.

We rage at every scandal. We protest. We demand.
And then, silence. Politicians return, wealthier than before.

Accountability is temporary. Impunity is permanent.

How many more generations must inherit this curse before we finally break it?

Sa isang ordinaryong Pilipino, Nakakapagod na. Nakakasawa na. Nakakamanhid na. Nahati na ang mga pilipino, ganon at ganon pa din! 

@adpr87law @jesusfalcis @teta_limcangco @kikopangilinan @risahontiveros @manayleila @ChelDiokno @lenirobredo @legallyzen @profcielomagno @IanEsguerra

🔴Where is Stable aiming?

@stable  isn’t just another blockchain payment project.
The market Stable is targeting is the global economy where USDT works like real money.

🟡 Global Remittance Market
When you send money to family or friends overseas,
banks often charge 5–10% in fees.
And sometimes it takes days for the money to arrive.

Stable offers gas-free transfers + sub-second finality.
For example, let’s say you’re sending $100 in tuition to your family in the Philippines.
With Stable, it costs zero fees and arrives instantly.

🟡 Everyday Payments
Stable is also built for small, everyday transactions.
Think of buying a cup of coffee, shopping online, or paying at a convenience store.

As long as you hold USDT, you can pay just like using a card.
The Stable Wallet is designed to be simple and intuitive so anyone can use it.
For example, if you buy a $3 drink at a convenience store,
you won’t end up paying $5 because of high fees anymore.

🟡 Enterprise Settlements
Enterprises move millions of dollars every single day.
But on today’s blockchains, congestion causes delays
and transaction fees are unpredictable.

Stable solves this with Guaranteed Blockspace for enterprises.
It also uses a Transfer Aggregator to bundle large transactions together.
For example, if a company needs to send salaries to 100 overseas branches,
Stable makes it much faster and cheaper.

🟡 DeFi and Crypto-Native Market
USDT already lives on Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and other chains.
Stable allows these assets to move in through the USDT Cross-Chain Bridge.

And because it’s 100% EVM-compatible, existing DeFi apps, NFTs, and even games can run directly on Stable.
So Stable isn’t just about payments it can also become the DeFi hub centered around USDT.

👉 In the end, Stable is building a USDT-only financial operating system.
The vision is simple: anyone, anywhere, should be able to do all their financial activities with just USDT.
